This prompt didn't match any scripted scenario, so I'm responding with the default simulation.

I'm the **static test backend** at `/ws/test`: no database, no provider, no model. Each prompt is matched against the JSON files in `data/simulation/`, and the first matching file's scripted response is played back — with thinking blocks, streamed content, and (when scripted) real tool execution against the workspace.

### Scripted scenarios available right now

| Try typing | What happens |
|---|---|
| `hello` | Friendly greeting + scenario map |
| `create a fastapi app` | **build** → full project scaffold; **plan** → build plan, no files |
| `design an api` | Complete REST API spec written to `docs/api.md` |
| `refactor this` | **build** → messy module analyzed, rewritten, verified; **plan** → refactoring plan |
| `make a plan` | Phased implementation plan saved to `PLAN.md` |
| `analyze this file` | Structured code review with severity ratings and fixes |

### How to script a new response

Add a file to `data/simulation/`, e.g. `data/simulation/my-topic.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "my-topic",
  "match": { "contains": "my topic" },
  "mode": "round_robin",
  "responses": [
    {
      "reasoning": "A short reasoning block shown as a thinking event.",
      "content": "The streamed reply.",
      "chunk_size": 3,
      "delay_ms": 20,
      "tool_calls": [
        { "tool": "file_write", "params": { "path": "out.txt", "content": "hi" } }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`match` supports `exact` (case-insensitive equality), `contains` (substring), and an optional `mode` (`build`/`plan`) that restricts the file to one session mode; `mode` at the top level sets the response picker (`round_robin`, `sequence`, or `random`). Simulation files reload on every prompt, so edits apply immediately.
